messages:
maria: heads up, ruby sample app onboarding got a UX footgun. when users install with `bundle install --binstubs` and run `bin/ruby sample_app.rb` our quickstart silently fails with a 401 (missing Authorization header). anyone seen this pattern?
kevin: oof yeah that can happen. binstubs sometimes run without loading project `.env`. what's the error blob?
maria: just `Unauthorized: missing Authorization header` from the SDK call. README only suggests exporting REDWOOD_API_KEY but we don't surface a clear hint. repro steps:
```
$ bundle install --binstubs
$ bin/ruby sample_app.rb
# => 401 Unauthorized
```
sam_ci: i observed a similar failure in the ruby-quickstart CI matrix earlier (job 7). rerun fixed it because the job uses `bundle exec ruby` by default. linking job: https://ci.internal/ci/786/job/7
julia: simple UX win: detect missing auth in bootstrap and print an actionable message like "Set REDWOOD_API_KEY or run with `bundle exec ruby` or use binstub-aware env loader". can be tiny but saves new users time.
kevin: i'll open a micro-PR: (1) improve error text when ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] missing, include workarounds; (2) add README snippet recommending `bundle exec` if using env file; (3) small unit test that clears ENV and asserts message.
pr-bot: opened #2401 by kevin: "ruby-quickstart: clearer auth message for bundler binstubs"
maria: please also mention `~/.config/redwood/token.json` fallback for devs using refresh token helpers.
kevin: added that note and a short inline comment in sample_app.rb. pushed a small fixup per review.
sam_ci: re-ran matrix, ruby-quickstart job now stable. :thumbsup:
julia: i'll update onboarding checklist and ping docs to mirror the README tweak.
maria: thanks all. i'll drop a short post in #new-hires to reduce future confusion.
